**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user attended a guided tour at the Natural History Museum.
- [FACT] The user was impressed by the fossil collection on display, especially the new T-Rex skeleton.
- [RELATIONSHIP] The user's dad accompanied them on the visit to the Natural History Museum.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is looking for information on dinosaurs, specifically the T-Rex.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The T-Rex roamed North America during the Late Cretaceous period, around 68-65 million years ago.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The T-Rex's habitat was likely a mix of forests, rivers, and coastal areas, with a subtropical to temperate climate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex was an apex predator with exceptional eyesight, powerful legs, and a formidable bite force.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex had the strongest bite of any dinosaur, with a force of around 6-9 tons per square inch (psi).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Fossil evidence suggests that T-Rex had feathers, which might have been used for display or insulation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex might have used ambush tactics for hunting and was likely a scavenger as well.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There is evidence suggesting T-Rex might have lived in small family groups.
- [PREFERENCE] The user expressed interest in learning about other dinosaurs that co-existed with the T-Rex.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable herbivorous dinosaurs that co-existed with T-Rex include Edmontosaurus, Triceratops, Ankylosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Hadrosaurus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Edmontosaurus could grow up to 12 meters (40 feet) in length and had a distinctive crest on its head.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Edmontosaurus crest might have been used for display, as a resonating chamber, for thermoregulation, or as a sensory organ.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Edmontosaurus was a herbivore that likely fed on ferns, cycads, conifers, and fruits.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Edmontosaurus had a beak-like snout and dental batteries for processing plant material.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum is planning an exhibit titled "Hadrosaurs: The Duck-Billed Giants of the Cretaceous" scheduled to open in about six months.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The exhibit will feature a nearly complete Edmontosaurus skeleton, hadrosaur skin impressions, an interactive beak simulation, life-sized hadrosaur models, and a fossil preparation lab.
